subject: Sustained 5xx & p95 latency on Lyra on-prem cluster — urgent remediation
messages:
From: Maya Singh <ops@lyrathx.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Clement Park <cto@lyrathx.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production p95/5xx surge - Lyra private cluster

Hi Stephanie,

We're seeing a sustained increase in p95 latency (from ~180ms to ~1.2s) and periodic 502/503 spikes across our on-prem inference cluster since early this morning. Error rates peak during short bursts of traffic but the baseline has also shifted up. This is impacting our clinical UI and a number of background batch jobs.

We opened a runbook ticket (PD-lyra-118) and collected logs/trace IDs; attaching a tarball with sample logs and the most recent heap dump. We're running Redwood Private v1.9.2 with the recommended quantization profile.

Can we get an immediate triage? Our CTO Clement Park is looped in and would like a concise remediation plan and ETA.

Attachments: lyra_logs_1205.tar.gz, heap-profile.json

Thanks,
Maya Singh
SRE — Lyra Therapeutics
ops@lyrathx.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com>
To: Maya Singh <ops@lyrathx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production p95/5xx surge - Lyra private cluster

Maya — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts.

Quick plan: I'm scheduling a triage call in 30 minutes with our on-call infra lead (Aditya) and CS engineer (Marissa). We need the following pre-call if you can:
- host-level top output (dstat/top) during a spike
- the slow trace ids you referenced (for kv-cache/attention behavior)
- current autoscaling and batch window settings

From past incidents, sustained p95 jumps + 5xxs on Private often correlate to: kernel/non-optimal AVX instruction fallback, a mis-sized batching window, or an unexpected token-length distribution causing KV cache churn. We'll validate all three quickly.

If the exec wants a temporary safety valve, Marissa will propose a hosted fallback routing for low-priority routes to reduce pressure.

Call: https://meet.redwood.com/steph-lyra-triage (10:35 PT).

-Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales (Escalations) — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2027 10:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production p95/5xx surge - Lyra private cluster

Maya / team — I'll be on the triage. A few items I'm bringing:
- quick diagnostic checklist (CPU steal, kernel logs for CPU microcode/thermal events, NVMe IO wait)
- small patch to reduce batch window and enable more aggressive prefix caching (safe for 1.9.x)
- fallback-routing.sh (small script) that temporarily redirects lower-priority endpoints to our hosted pool and preserves auth headers

If you prefer not to route to hosted, we can still do a kernel-level instrumentation pass and push a runtime flag that reduces eager KV eviction for 24 hours. That usually cuts p95 by 30–40% while we do a deeper kernel/quantization pass.

Attaching: fallback-routing.sh

—Marissa
Customer Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
From: Maya Singh <ops@lyrathx.com>

Subject: Re: Production p95/5xx surge - Lyra private cluster

Thanks all — joining the call now. Couple of quick data points:
- Trace IDs: trace-5a2f, trace-5a33, trace-5a4d included in the tarball; they show long attention kernel times for longer prompts during spikes.
- We are at 80% of node capacity; yesterday's deployment increased token-length defaults for a new beta feature.
- Clement: we're putting you on the thread so execs are aware — his ask: explicit ETA for mitigation and whether a temporary traffic-shed is required.

We can accept hosted fallback for non-PHI endpoints, but any routing requires a short IRT for compliance review.

Maya
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production p95/5xx surge - Lyra private cluster — exec brief

Rishi — quick exec summary and ask:

Lyra's on-prem cluster (v1.9.2, quant-profile=opt-std) is experiencing a sustained p95 jump (~180ms -> 1.2s) plus intermittent 5xx spikes during short bursts after they rolled out a prompt-length change. Their cluster is at ~80% capacity which amplifies KV cache churn.

We propose a two-track remediation:
1) Immediate (hours): apply runtime flag to reduce KV eviction aggressiveness + reduce batch_window to 8ms and enable conservative prefix caching. This is low-risk and reversible. If approved, Marissa will shepherd and Aditya will sign off on the ssh/playbook.
2) Short-term (24–72h): push a micro-kernel tweak from infra that reduces attention kernel latency on the affected instruction path; requires a coordinated restart of inference workers during a maintenance window.

Lyra execs want an ETA and clarity on SLA impact. They are okay with hosted fallback for non-PHI routes but compliance signoff will add latency to that route.

Attachments: heatmap.png (latency heatmap from 12/5)

Asking for greenlight to proceed with (1) immediately and commit engineering time for (2) within 48h.

-Stephanie Nguyen
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production p95/5xx surge - Lyra private cluster — exec brief

Thanks for the succinct summary, Stephanie. Approve immediate (1). Marissa/Aditya: make the KV-eviction change and batch_window reduction the top priority — coordinate with Lyra for a short maintenance window today.

For (2) I want a proposed list of code-change candidates with risk assessments by EOD tomorrow; if it's a kernel/path issue we'll pull in runtime infra and schedule the micro-kernel patch in a controlled rollout. If Lyra is at 80% capacity, provisioned capacity guidance should be part of the postmortem and timeline for permanent changes.

Also copy legal and compliance on any hosted-fallback plan; if they take that route we need a swift SOC/KMS attestation.

Rishi
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com
